content: TAS2R10, also known as taste receptor type 2 member 10, is a protein encoded by the TAS2R10 gene in humans. This protein is part of the family of candidate taste receptors, which belong to the G-protein-coupled receptor superfamily. These receptors are specifically expressed in the taste receptor cells located in the tongue and palate epithelia. Within the genome, these receptors are organized into clusters and are genetically linked to loci that influence the perception of bitterness in both mice and humans. Functional expression studies have demonstrated that these receptors respond to bitter-tasting compounds. The TAS2R10 gene is mapped to the taste receptor gene cluster on chromosome 12p13. In addition to its role in taste perception, TAS2R10 is expressed in the smooth muscle of human airways, along with several other bitter taste receptors. When activated in these airway smooth muscle cells, TAS2R10 triggers an increase in intracellular calcium ion levels. This rise in calcium subsequently leads to the opening of potassium channels, which hyperpolarize the cell membrane and induce relaxation of the smooth muscle. As a result, activation of these receptors promotes bronchodilation.
